feed.description: Investing conversations for normal humans: frameworks, risk, and the habits that matter more than predictions.
feed.title: Long Horizon Notes

bullets: Policy decisions look obvious in hindsight and impossible in real time — a framing that clarifies which tradeoffs are being made.
Forward guidance only works if the market believes you will follow through; the second-order effect is the part most people miss.
Risk management at the Fed is mostly about not breaking the institution — a pattern observed across three different teams.
Reliability of policy signal matters more than the policy itself; once internalized, the rest of the decisions get easier.
The failure mode of policy signal reliability is harder to spot outside of Morningstar class tooling — Bloomberg is one platform where it shows up cleanly.
The tradeoffs around reliability crosscut everything covered in the conversation, making it the central lens for evaluating policy decisions.
A concrete next step is to pick one of the covered ideas and run it for two weeks — the rest is iteration.
